text:
sam: FYI customer (acme) reports monthly credits hit 0 earlier than their timezone expected. they saw UI=0 at 00:00 local, but their tenant tz is PST. asking why reset happened ~2 hours early. attaching logs next.

alice: can you paste the tenant id + correlation id from their API 429?

sam: tenant=acme-prod-23, correlation=cor_0a1b2c3d, customer saw repeated 429s on long streaming job. they said it happened right after a reconnect.

maya: quick checklist: confirm tenant timezone in billing table, check refill scheduler logs, and look for any DST/offset flags in the refill job. sometimes cache invalidation shows zero in UI while backend replenished.

leo: repro attempt steps I'm going to try:
```
# open long streaming websocket, consume tokens until near-zero
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"model":"rwd-2-large","prompt":"x"}'\n# force reconnect, check for 429
```

sam: customer timeline: connected at 23:50 PST, heavy generation, reconnect at 23:59:10, API returned 429 at 23:59:12, UI showed zero at 00:00:00, but backend billing logs show refill at 01:00:00 UTC (which is 00:00 PST) — they're seeing it appear as earlier though.

billing-bot: Invoice/billing service note: refill job run id=refill-2026-03-01-00 triggered at 01:00:00Z for tenant acme-prod-23.

alice: hmm. that suggests UI cache showed zero before the refill propagated to the UI. can you check the cache-invalidation logs and edge TTLs? pagecache invalidation sometimes lags after refill apply.

maya: also check whether the customer's account has "staggered-refill" flag — that can cause visible zero on long connections until reconnect.

leo: i pulled the refill scheduler log:
```
[2026-03-01T01:00:00Z] refill: tenant=acme-prod-23; scheduled=true; run_id=refill-2026-03-01-00; status=success; delta=+100000
[2026-03-01T01:00:01Z] cache: publish tenant=acme-prod-23; key=credits:acme-prod-23; ttl=30s
```
But I also see an earlier cache write at 2026-03-01T00:59:12Z setting credits=0 for websocket-session entries.

sam: customer claims they saw UI=0 at 00:00:00 local. could be rounding/clock skew on their machine + our UI snapshot.

eng-oncall: @noah can you weigh in? any scheduled change recently to refill window or DST handling?

noah: checking — we shipped a scheduler patch last week to normalize refill times to tenant local midnight. a bug in tz normalization caused some tenants with explicit PST config to get midnight applied twice in edge cases (off-by-one hour) during DST-rollover flag toggles. I see acme-prod-23 matched that path.

noah: root cause: refill scheduler used naive localtime conversion when tenant had legacy tz flag. patch: https://git.internal/redwood/refill/commit/3f7a9c9 — will backport hotfix to prod scheduler.

eng-oncall: scheduling hotfix now, rolling to region us-west-2. deploy ETA 30m. will also purge stale pagecache entries for affected tenants.

sam: proposed customer reply: "we found a bug in our monthly refill scheduler that can cause an off-by-one hour visible reset for some tenants during tz/DST transitions. we're deploying a hotfix and clearing caches — your credits will appear correctly shortly. apologies for the disruption; we'll follow up once fixed." ok to send? :+1:

alice: :+1: send and cc support-billing. include repro steps and correlation id.

sam: sent to customer, copying timeline and repro. customer acknowledged and is waiting for update.

leo: adding quick mitigations in case others hit this: 1) detect long-lived streams and refresh TTL on reconnect, 2) proactively invalidate pagecache after refill apply, 3) alert if refill time != expected by > 5m. I'll open tickets.

noah: created ENG-REFILL-512 for hotfix + cache purge runbook.

sam: thanks all — keeping thread open until rollout done.
